name: Water
use: The universal solvent and the most common reference compound in stoichiometry problems.

name: Carbon dioxide
use: Produced by respiration and combustion; used in carbonated drinks and fire extinguishers.

name: Oxygen
use: Diatomic gas essential for respiration and combustion.

name: Nitrogen
use: Makes up about 78% of air and is used as an inert atmosphere in food packaging.

name: Ozone
use: Forms the stratospheric ozone layer and is used to disinfect water.

name: Ammonia
use: Starting material for most nitrogen fertilizers via the Haber process.

name: Methane
use: Main component of natural gas.

name: Propane
use: Bottled fuel gas for cooking and heating.

name: Ethylene
use: Plant hormone that ripens fruit and the monomer for polyethylene.

name: Ethanol
use: Alcohol in beverages and a common lab solvent and fuel additive.

name: Acetone
use: Fast-evaporating solvent found in nail polish remover.

name: Benzene
use: Aromatic hydrocarbon used as a feedstock for plastics and dyes.

name: Acetic acid
use: The acid in vinegar.

name: Glucose
use: Blood sugar and the main energy source for cells.

name: Sucrose
use: Table sugar refined from sugarcane and sugar beet.

name: Aspirin
use: Pain reliever and anti-inflammatory drug (acetylsalicylic acid).

name: Caffeine
use: Stimulant found in coffee and tea.

name: Urea
use: High-nitrogen fertilizer and the main nitrogen waste in urine.

name: Hydrochloric acid
use: Strong acid found in stomach juice and used to clean steel.

name: Sulfuric acid
use: The most produced industrial chemical; used in fertilizers and car batteries.

name: Nitric acid
use: Strong oxidizing acid used to make nitrate fertilizers.

name: Phosphoric acid
use: Used in phosphate fertilizers and as an acidulant in soft drinks.

name: Sodium hydroxide
use: Caustic soda; used in soap making and drain cleaners.

name: Potassium hydroxide
use: Used in liquid soaps and alkaline batteries.

name: Calcium hydroxide
use: Slaked lime; used in mortar and to raise soil pH.

name: Sodium chloride
use: Table salt.

name: Potassium chloride
use: Potash fertilizer and a salt substitute.

name: Calcium chloride
use: De-icing agent and drying agent in labs.

name: Calcium carbonate
use: Limestone and chalk; also used as an antacid.

name: Sodium carbonate
use: Washing soda used in glassmaking and detergents.

name: Sodium bicarbonate
use: Baking soda; a leavening agent and mild antacid.

name: Sodium sulfate
use: Filler in powdered detergents and used in paper pulping.

name: Magnesium sulfate
use: Anhydrous Epsom salt; used as a drying agent and magnesium fertilizer.

name: Copper(II) sulfate
use: Fungicide and algaecide; the white anhydrous powder turns blue when hydrated.

name: Iron(II) sulfate
use: Iron supplement and a treatment for iron-deficient soils.

name: Barium sulfate
use: Insoluble salt used as a contrast agent in X-ray imaging.

name: Potassium nitrate
use: Fertilizer and a food preservative.

name: Silver nitrate
use: Used in the classic chloride test and in early photography.

name: Ammonium nitrate
use: High-nitrogen fertilizer.

name: Ammonium sulfate
use: Nitrogen and sulfur fertilizer for alkaline soils.

name: Lead(II) nitrate
use: Common lab reagent in precipitation experiments.

name: Aluminium sulfate
use: Flocculant used to clear drinking water.

name: Potassium permanganate
use: Strong oxidizer used in titrations and water treatment.

name: Potassium dichromate
use: Orange oxidizing agent used in redox titrations.

name: Copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate
use: Blue vitriol; the bright blue crystals seen in school labs.

name: Magnesium sulfate heptahydrate
use: The hydrated form sold as Epsom salt for baths.

name: Iron(III) oxide
use: Rust and the red pigment in many paints.

name: Magnesium oxide
use: Heat-resistant refractory material and an antacid.

name: Zinc oxide
use: White pigment and the active ingredient in mineral sunscreen.

name: Silicon dioxide
use: Quartz and sand; the main raw material for glass.

name: Hydrogen peroxide
use: Mild antiseptic and bleaching agent.
